title: Playing the Sheraton Waikiki and singing for dancers
summary: He has worked five years at the Sheraton Waikiki in a quartet, singing more because dancers want lyrics.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: And for things like Dick Gibson's
And you come back (inaudible) -- and how often do you come back?

Oh, only about once a year. But since I've been on this particular job, I can only get away once a year. You know, I would have come back more often, but sometimes you got a steady job, you can't get away. I'm not getting rich on this job, but it -- in the meantime it's a living, you know. It keeps me playing.
I work at Sheraton, the Waikiki Hotel, you know.
And you've been there how long?
Five years. I just signed a new one year contract. But I work up on the 30th floor, kind of over
the ocean, and it's glass enclosed, the room is. It's a nice room.
How big a group is it?

Just three guys and myself. Got a piano player, and he plays organ once in a while and piano and drums, and a guy plays the electric bass. I don't care too much for the electric bass, but I like the upright bass, you know, better, but --
Yeah, I like it better. One of the reasons I got this guy, he sings fairly well, you know. When you got a little group, you got to utilize every little thing that you possibly can, you know.
Well, you do singing too, don't you?
Yeah, I do a lot of singing up there because --
As well as ----- but you had him singing, too, (inaudible).
-- there's dancing there. Well, we sing some four way things too, like some of the things I did with Lunceford, you know. We do some of those things.

But when you're playing for dancing, you got -- you have to usually do more singing because they want to hear lyrics, you know, a guy dancing with his chick out there, he wants to hear some lyrics and things. So you -- actually you do more singing than you would ordinarily when you -- if
you're playing for dancing, you know, unless you got a band like Basie's band that's really playing for swingers, you know.
